evidence.excerpt: Biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films prepared at draw ratios of 5×5 to 9×9 were characterised for oxygen transmission rate (OTR) using a coulometric sensor method at 23 °C and 0 % relative humidity. Wide-angle X-ray scattering confirmed an increase in crystallinity from 42 % to 61 % with rising draw ratio. OTR values decreased from 1840 to 890 cm³/(m²·day·bar) over the same range. DSC measurements showed that lamellar thickness, as estimated by the Thomson–Gibbs equation, increased from 8.2 to 14.7 nm. A linear correlation was established between the reciprocal of lamellar thickness and OTR, consistent with a tortuous-path diffusion model. FTIR-ATR band ratios at 998/973 cm⁻¹ were used as an independent crystallinity index and agreed within 4 % with WAXS results. The findings provide quantitative guidance for process optimisation of BOPP films where oxygen barrier is the primary constraint.
